for c in ['application','instance_family']:
    p=d.pivot_table(index='date',columns=c,values='unblended_cost',aggfunc='sum')

    print(x.head(3));print(x.tail(4))
p=d.pivot_table(index='date',columns='instance_family',values='unblended_cost',aggfunc='sum')
print(p[['23zHd9pKgs','qtVJ1PKHrR']].loc['2025-09-20':].round(0).T.to_string())

steps.content:
On 2025-10-13, the anomalous cost for account frHBxlu came from one resource: instance family **qtVJ1PKHrR**. It runs only under application eTs and cloud service nOcDI.

- **What changed:** this instance family usually costs about $66–$94 a day. On 2025-10-13 it jumped to about $329 and stayed there on 10-14 and 10-15. Compared with the previous Monday (10-06), that is about $253 more, the biggest rise of any instance family or application in the account. It hasn't gone back down, so this is a real cost increase that is still running.
- **A bigger increase that is not the cause:** the account total rose from about $8,478 on 10-12 to $10,316 on 10-13. Most of that jump came from instance family 23zHd9pKgs (application b7h, service meFyk), which went from about $35 to $1,635. That family follows the same weekly pattern every week: about $1,635 on Monday and Tuesday, $417 Wednesday to Friday, and $35 on weekends. It did exactly the same on 9-22, 9-29 and 10-06, so it's a normal weekly cycle and not part of the anomaly.

<answer>{"resource": [{"name": "qtVJ1PKHrR", "type": "Instance Family"}]}</answer>
